content.text:
You are a veteran Capcom NES pixel artist and art director for Mega Man 2-3. You are shown ONE small enemy sprite,
at 1x (true size, left) and enlarged with nearest-neighbour scaling (right), on a neutral grey-blue background
that is not part of the sprite.

The sprite is supposed to be this enemy:
"A small floating robot squid, Blooper-like, that swims along at and after Mega Man in pulses (tentacles gather, then thrust). It is a swimming mine: when it gets close its eyes flash red, then it explodes."
Intended size: about 16x16 to 20x20 px. Game: Mega Man 2-3 (NES).

Judge whether it is a convincing authentic NES Mega Man enemy that matches the description. Be calibrated:
authentic Capcom enemy sprites score about 90-95; competent fan art about 60-70; amateur or AI-looking pixel art
about 30-45. Do not reward or punish a sprite for being recognisable; judge what you see.

Criteria, 0-10 each:
- authenticity: could ship unchanged in MM2/MM3 (Capcom conventions, not "modern pixel art")
- description_fidelity: matches the description (body, features, role)
- readability_1x: the silhouette and features read instantly at true size
- pixel_craft: 1-px black outlines used the Capcom way, clean clusters, no jaggies, orphans, dithering or noise
- palette_discipline: NES colours, flat shading with at most one highlight, about 3 colours + transparent per 8x8 tile
- appeal: charm and character in the Capcom manner

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"subscores": {"authenticity": n, "description_fidelity": n, "readability_1x": n, "pixel_craft": n,
  "palette_discipline": n, "appeal": n},
 "score": 0-100 overall,
 "verdict": "convincing" or "not_convincing",
 "issues": ["specific, located problems"],
 "fixes": ["specific pixel-level fixes"]}

message.content: {"subscores":{"authenticity":5,"description_fidelity":8,"readability_1x":7,"pixel_craft":6,"palette_discipline":5,"appeal":6},"score":62,"verdict":"not_convincing","issues":["The oversized rectangular white side lobes make the body read more like a helmet or crab than a compact floating squid.","The lower silhouette is crowded: cyan tentacles merge with heavy black horizontal and vertical bars at 1x.","Black interior areas are too broad and geometric for typical MM2/MM3 outlining, especially beneath and between the eyes.","White, cyan, dark cyan, red, and black occur in close proximity, creating questionable NES sprite-palette/tile usage without obvious overlay planning.","The two square red eyes look mechanically pasted into matching black sockets rather than integrated into a charming Capcom face.","Tentacles lack a clearly readable gathered-versus-thrust pose, weakening the pulsing-swim concept."],"fixes":["Narrow each white side lobe by 1-2 pixels and round the upper mantle into a simpler domed squid silhouette.","Replace the thick lower black bar with separated 1-pixel outline clusters so negative space remains between the tentacles.","Reduce the eyes to smaller white or red 1-2 pixel cores inside cleaner black sockets; reserve red for a deliberate flash overlay frame.","Limit the base sprite to black, white, and cyan, using dark cyan only as a single compact shadow cluster or removing it entirely.","Separate the three lower appendages by at least one transparent pixel and make their curves consistent rather than stair-stepped.","Create two animation frames: inward-curled tentacles for gathering and a narrow, extended rearward cluster for thrust.","Remove isolated right-angle interior blocks and use single-pixel Capcom-style contour notches to suggest machinery without filling the body with black."]}
